correctness.rationale: The exact normalized response, a real exponent strictly above one and all positive budget/scale quantifiers are stated. Differentiation yields the unique inflection point and local threshold. All off-center stationary equations are equivalent to \(N=Q_p(z)\) with positive auxiliary parameter. The proof rigorously establishes Q_p strictly increasing from the local threshold to infinity using \(H(s)=(s\coth s)'\), its increasing derivative and strictly decreasing \(H(s)/s\); the inequality is independently derived, not assumed. Thus there is no missing off-center critical point. Endpoint signs and symmetry give complete extrema classification, including the flat-at-quadratic-order equality at the local threshold. Direct payoff subtraction gives unique global switch and strict \(N_{\mathrm{loc}}<N_{\mathrm{glob}}\). A controlled Taylor expansion proves the exponent-independent leading square-root coefficient. Exact the quadratic exponent radicals independently check the barrier. Attached self-contained numerical diagnostics were executed and passed; they are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The shape-constrained ecology problem is natural: fixed total prey spread over exactly two equal-area patches with identical learning/Type III feeding predators. Local curvature predicts an even-split local optimum before that allocation actually surpasses complete clumping globally. Proving the two thresholds strictly separated for all real a real exponent strictly above one, excluding all other stationary points by a nonstandard hyperbolic monotonicity lemma, and deriving a universal square-root bifurcation coefficient supplies a motivated structural classification rather than routine substitution or a narrow arbitrary numerical fact. The discontinuous global switch and exact the quadratic exponent barrier are interpretable mathematical benchmarks. Scope is not expanded to dynamical ecology.
